newsitem.title: PERU: Peru court revokes critical TV mogul's nationality.
newsitem.headline: Peru court revokes critical TV mogul's nationality.

text.p: A court has revoked the Peruvian nationality of the Israeli-born owner of a television station that has been fiercely critical of President Alberto Fujimori's administration, legal officials said on Friday.

The widely expected ruling -- upholding an earlier government decree -- means Baruch Ivcher will have to give up his Frecuencia Latina station because Peruvian law forbids foreigners from owning local TV channels.
Ivcher plans to appeal the decision. But while his ownership rights are under legal dispute, pro-government minority shareholders of Frecuencia Latina are in control of the station's administration.

The government moved to revoke Ivcher's nationality last month after he allowed his station to air a series of reports alleging abuses of power by the security forces. The scandals, involving torture and phonetapping, damaged Fujimori's popularity.

But the government's claim that Ivcher committed administrative "irregularities" when he obtained Peruvian nationality in 1984 unleashed a barrage of media criticism. The case also provided a lightning rod for an increasingly hostile public to voice its dissatisfaction with Fujimori, causing him to tumble to record lows of around 20 percent in the polls.

The president has since recovered ground after granting wage hikes and public reaction to the court's ruling on Friday was muted. A new survey on Friday of 400 Peruvians by local pollster Datum gave Fujimori a 35.8 percent approval rating.
